newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria not behind attack on activist, minister.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria not behind attack on activist, minister.

text.p: A Nigerian opposition leader's claim that the military government tried to assassinate him was on Wednesday rejected by a cabinet minister.

The vice-chairman of the opposition NADECO group, Senator Abraham Adesanya told reporters he escaped an assassination attempt on Tuesday when unknown gunmen shot at him in his car. He accused the government of being responsible for the attack.
"There is no reason whatsoever for government to assassinate Adesanya," special duties minister Wada Nas told BBC radio.
"I think he just wants publicity and he is getting it now."
Adesanya, 74, alleged at a news conference in Lagos last week that he and Michael Ajasin, the octogenarian leader of NADECO, were marked out for elimination.

NADECO (National Democratic Coalition) is the umbrella organisation of pro-democracy groups that back Moshood Abiola, the presumed winner of a 1993 presidential poll annulled by a previous army government, who has been detained since 1994.
Nas, who has many times accused NADECO of sabotage against the government, said Adesanya should search within the ranks of NADECO for the culprits in the attempt on his life.
"Maybe his associates are suspecting him of duping them out of the money they are getting from overseas from the people who are sponsoring them," he said.

Nigeria has been rocked by three unexplained bomb attacks since December that have killed three soldiers and wounded dozens of others in Lagos. The government blames the exiled opposition, which it says is linked to NADECO, for the bombings.
